messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: latency.slo.burn HIGH for service=redwood-serving hotpath=generate (p99 > 1200ms for 5m). PagerDuty incident PD-9271 created and auto-paged rotation.
PagerDuty: Incoming page PD-9271 -> oncall=jamiemon (primary).
jamie: acked the page. looking now. any customer-facing errors?
jamie: getting p95 ~220ms but p99 spikes to ~1.3s on generate-hotpath in us-west-2. graphs: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving/latency?panel=hotpath
sofia: noted, I'm joining. do we have recent deploys to hotpath?
kevin: there was a tiny runtime change 38m ago to KV cache eviction heuristics (PR #5420). it touched our prefix caching TTL logic. rolling back would be quick but want confirmation.
jamie: can someone paste the top traces?
kevin: copying spans:
```
trace_id=abcd1234 service=generate node=gpu-12 duration=1287ms step=kv_fetch
  step=kernel_launch wait=800ms
  step=quantize commit=200ms
```

kevin: looks like KV fetch latency is high and kernels are queueing. GPU mem pressure on a few nodes.
sofia: resource panel shows 3/12 gpus in the pool hitting 95% memory, OOMs not consistent but heavy swapping.
jamie: customer impact? any errors thrown to clients?
kevin: no 5xx spike, mostly tail latency. threads show many requests falling back to synchronous redis KV access. dedicated customers on ReservedPool-A are seeing p99 ~1.4s. Hosted API OK.
sofia: summary: p99 latency SLO burning for Dedicated/reserved in us-west-2. cause hypothesis: KV cache eviction change + uneven shard placement -> GPU memory spike -> kernel queuing.
jamie: mitigation plan: 1) revert PR #5420 on runtime to restore previous TTL, 2) temporarily scale up reserved pool by +2 nodes, 3) enable model-fallback route to a smaller variant for new requests, 4) engage oncall for rollout.
kevin: starting rollback now. kubectl apply -f rollout-revert.yaml
```
kubectl -n serving set image deployment/runtime runtime=image/redwood/runtime:2026-02-24-rev
```

kevin: rollback submitted, rolling update to 2 nodes at a time. ETA ~4m.
sofia: scaling reserved pool: hitting autoscaler API now.
sofia: `POST /api/v1/pools/ReservedPool-A/scale` -> +2 gpus, expected warm-up 3m.
jamie: enabling fallback route for hotpath: set route weight generate-hotpath -> generate-hotpath-small 30%
jamie: `PATCH /routes/generate-hotpath` -> weight_small=30

incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-9271: ack by jamie at 1846000150.
PagerDuty: PD-9271 escalated to rotation-level-2 at 1846000212 (no ack from level-2).
sofia: after scaling started, I see memory drop on previously hot nodes. p99 coming down to ~820ms.
kevin: rollback completed on 6 nodes at 1846000298. kernel queue times reduced in traces.
jamie: good. continue to monitor for 15m. set Slack pin to this thread.
sofia: running quick smoke on dedicated customers: 3 sample tenants, 50 concurrent reqs each. results: p99 ~420-600ms. still above target but trending down.
kevin: leaving fallback route in place for another 10m, will ramp down to 0% if stable.
jamie: recorded mitigation actions in runbook: https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/PD-9271
sofia: customer impact note: no 5xx; increased tail latency affected throughput for certain reserved workloads resulting in slower responses but no data loss. likely noticed by teams using strict latency SLAs.
jamie: assigning follow-ups: kevin to investigate cache TTL regression root cause, sofia to improve autoscaler buffer for reserved pools, jamie to notify account team for any dedicated customers in us-west-2.
kevin: quick note: I see one node with slow nvlink transfers; collecting dmesg and nvtop logs, attaching below.
```
# nvlink stats
GPU0 <-> GPU1 errors: 0
PCIe retransmits: 12
```

sofia: paging schedule: I'm taking handoff at 1846000380 and will own until 1846001800. jamie: stand down?
jamie: handing off, I'm stepping out in 10. all actions handed off to sofia. keep this thread updated.
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-9271: acknowledged by sofia at 1846000390.
sofia: monitoring: p99 now hovering 360-520ms. keeping fallback route 10% for 5m, then remove if stable.
kevin: root cause triage note (short): cache TTL regression plus uneven shard placement when autoscaler removed one warm node earlier -> temporary memory pressure under burst. plan: add safety margin to autoscaler and revert TTL change permanently after regression test.
jamie: any need to open a customer-facing incident? product counters: small number of reserved tenants impacted with >500ms p99 for ~22m window. suggest targeted notification to account contacts rather than org-wide status.
sofia: agree. I'll draft a targeted note and post on #customer-impact.
kevin: will follow up with perf tests for different model sizes and sequence lengths to validate.
sofia: closing actions: 1) rollback verified, 2) autoscaler adjusted (temp buffer +1), 3) fallback route removed at 1846000448, 4) monitoring shows stabilization.
incident-bot: PD-9271 resolved automatically by system at 1846000460 (condition cleared).
jamie: thanks all. I'll add postmortem bullets and assign owners. :thumbsup:
